request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to the sheet now writes one line to the audit file in the order the request gives, and changes that are refused write nothing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**How it works (all on the server; the front end didn't need to change):**
- **Who made the change:** until now the server never kept the signed-in name. Signing in now stores it in the browser's HTTP session (`SessionController.java`). The add and edit endpoints for people and claims read it from there, so each browser context records its own user.
- **No line for a refused change:** I added `Audit.recordOnCommit` (`Audit.java`), which writes the line only after the database transaction commits. A change that fails validation, uses a name already taken, or hits the unique-name check in the database is rolled back, so no line is written. Any rule added later that throws inside the transaction gets the same behaviour.
- **The lines themselves:** `PersonService` writes `PERSON_ADDED` and `PERSON_EDITED`, and `ClaimService` writes `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED`. Claim lines look up the person's name. Amounts use the stored two-decimal value, the same one the screen shows, and dates are written as yyyy-mm-dd.

One behaviour change: adding or editing a person or claim without signing in first is now refused with a 400 error. That can't happen through the screen, which always signs in first.
